newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong stocks in London unchanged, banks active.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks in London unchanged, banks active.

text.p: Hong Kong shares were barely changed on Friday, weighed down by the languishing UK market but amid some interest in the banking sector, dealers said.
The Hang Seng London Reference index stood at 15,154.09 points, up a mere 0.27 points.
Earlier in the morning the Hang Seng index jumped 647.87 points, or 4.47 percent, to close at a new all-time high of 15,154.36 points as a wave of handover euphoria swept through the market.
"The banks were active, otherwise it was not that exiting", one trader said.
In the banking sector HSBC Holdings Plc was up HK$ 4.62 at HK$ 231.50. The stock closed in Hong Kong at HK$ 233, up HK$ 7.
HSBC was lifted by talk that its subsidiary Hang Seng Bank could get a major shareholder from the Chinese mainland, when Hong Kong returns to China on July 1.
Hang Seng Bank gained HK$ 12.5 to HK$ 109.875, compared with a close of HK$ 109.50 in Hong Kong.
Earlier HSBC dismissed the rumour, saying it would not change its shareholding in Hang Seng Bank.
